subject: Novus Health: dedicated capacity vs hosted & private — follow-up and sizing questions
messages:
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Manoj Reddy <manoj.reddy@novushealth.com>, Elena Garcia <elena.garcia@novushealth.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-20T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Novus Health: dedicated capacity vs hosted & private — quick recap + next steps

Thanks again for your time today — great conversation. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

- Primary use case: real-time clinical summarization and triage for inbound patient messages. Low latency required for clinician UX; some downstream batch jobs for analytics.
- Preliminary traffic estimate from the call: 50 TPS sustained during business hours, spikes to ~120 TPS in peak windows. Typical prompt size ~350 tokens, expected model output ~150 tokens (so ~500 tokens per request on average).
- Deployment modes under consideration: Hosted API for initial speed, Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput and cost control, Private VPC (on-prem optional later) for PHI regulatory requirements.
- Key constraints called out: HIPAA/PHI, customer-managed KMS, regional data residency, latency SLO of 150–200ms p50 for interactive flows.

Immediate next steps I propose: 
1) Sergio will share a capacity worksheet to capture exact TPS, concurrency, token distributions, and preferred GPUs so we can produce a sizing estimate.
2) Novus confirms whether PHI will be in-flight and at-rest (affects Private/Dedicated breakpoints).
3) Schedule a 30–45m tech deep-dive next week to align on batch vs real-time split and caching strategy.

Sergio — copying you to share the worksheet and any quick notes on GPU choices. Manoj/Elena — feel free to correct any items above.

Best,
Lauren Bishop
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: novus-poc-agenda.pdf (1.2MB)]

From: Manoj Reddy <manoj.reddy@novushealth.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Garcia <elena.garcia@novushealth.com>
Date: 2026-08-20T17:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Novus Health: dedicated capacity vs hosted & private — quick recap + next steps

Thanks Lauren — recap looks right. A couple clarifications from our side that will affect sizing: 

- The 50 TPS number is our initial target for triage during clinic hours only (8am–6pm ET). Outside those hours we expect ~5–8 TPS for background processing. Peak bursts (e.g., open enrollment or announcements) could push short-term spikes to 200 TPS for ~2–5 minutes.
- Token mix: about 30% of requests are short (<=128 tokens total), 55% are mid (256–512 tokens), and ~15% are long (>1024 tokens) mostly for full-note generation. Average request/response per call still ~500 tokens but with a heavy tail.
- Security: yes, PHI will be passed in payloads. We need VPC + customer KMS. Initially we'd prefer Dedicated in our cloud region, with Private on-prem as a later option if the compliance team insists.

I'll pull procurement into the thread separately to start paperwork once we have a sizing + cost estimate.

- Manoj
Director of Engineering, Novus Health
[Sent from mobile]

Subject: Redwood capacity worksheet + quick notes on GPU & concurrency assumptions

Hi Manoj / Elena — attaching the capacity worksheet Lauren mentioned. Filled in rows for the numbers Manoj provided; I also added two sizing scenarios so you can see tradeoffs:

Scenario A — Dedicated (cost-efficient, predictable):
- Target sustained TPS: 50
- Burst TPS: 200 (short windows)
- Average tokens/request: 500
- Concurrency target: 250 active connections
- Suggested GPU: H100 (80GB) for best latency at high concurrency; alternative A100-80GB if availability/cost constraints.
- Expected p50 latency estimate (common transformer model): ~110–160ms depending on batching and KV cache hit rate.

Scenario B — Hosted + Smart Routing (fast to start, avoid upfront commit):
- Start on hosted API for initial 50 TPS; route long-running heavy requests to a Dedicated pool or lower-cost model to prevent impact on latency.
- Recommend prefix caching for repeat prompts, and using smaller, quantized models for long-note generation.

Notes and asks from our side:
1) Please confirm whether long-note generation can be async (background) or must be interactive. Offloading those to batch reduces Dedicated GPU needs significantly.
2) If PHI is required on day 1 and customer-managed KMS is mandatory, Dedicated in your VPC (Private) or Redwood Private are viable — we'll need a security review and an MoU for KMS integration and network peering.

Attachment: redwood_capacity_worksheet_v2.xlsx (20KB) — worksheet includes per-model token estimates, concurrency formulas, and cost-by-sku tabs.

Feel free to edit the worksheet and push it back. If helpful, I can run a quick runbook showing estimated GPUs and monthly committed vCPU/GPU counts.

Thanks,
Sergio Alvarez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: redwood_capacity_worksheet_v2.xlsx (20KB)]

From: Elena Garcia <elena.garcia@novushealth.com>

Date: 2026-08-21T11:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood capacity worksheet + quick notes on GPU & concurrency assumptions

Appreciate the worksheet and notes — a few procurement/regulatory items from our side: 

- PHI: Our security team flags that PHI in payloads requires customer-managed KMS and network isolation. Please confirm Redwood Private supports HSM-backed KMS or point us to the KMS integration doc.
- Data residency: All stored artifacts must remain in us-east-1. Can Dedicated be pinned to that region for both runtime and logging?
- Contractual: procurement@novushealth.com — can you share standard SOC 2 + HIPAA addenda and any reference SLAs for p50/p95?

On the technical side: we can offload long-note generation to batch jobs (async) which should reduce the high-tail token load. That said, around 10–15% of our clinical edits will still be interactive and may be >1024 tokens. Curious whether the Dedicated H100 guidance you gave has sufficient memory headroom for mixed short/long workloads without excessive model switching.

If you can send the KMS/HSM integration notes and a pinned-region deployment outline, procurement will start paperwork.

Thanks,
Elena Garcia
Head of Product, Novus Health

Subject: INTERNAL: Novus Health sizing recap & ask — pricing guidance + security path

Internal recap and asks (Novus Health / NVH-2026-0820-01):

Summary: Novus wants Dedicated in us-east-1 if PHI required day 1. Traffic profile: 50TPS sustained (8am–6pm ET), bursts to 200TPS, avg ~500 tokens with 15% long requests >1024; they can offload ~85% of long-note generation to async but require interactive edits for ~15%.

Technical recommendation from Sergio: prefer H100 80GB for concurrency/latency; A100 80GB acceptable if cost/availability tradeoff needed. We should provide two commitment scenarios: 6-month pilot (lower commit, higher unit cost) and 12-month committed capacity (discounted). Pricing should include options: Dedicated reserved (Redwood-managed), Dedicated in-customer VPC (network peering + KMS integration), and Redwood Private (full private control plane) for strict PHI.

Action items: 
- Marcus: can you draft a price sketch for the three options (pilot/12mo) and include estimated monthly GPU counts from Sergio's worksheet? Please prioritize H100 pricing and fallback to A100.
- Monica: please prep a HIPAA/SOC2 + KMS integration summary we can share with procurement; include typical MoU language for KMS/HSM and network peering steps.
- Sergio: if you can add a small-run example (estimated GPUs, token cost, expected p50/p95 per scenario) into the worksheet, we can include that in the commercial proposal.

I'll coordinate follow-up meeting with Novus for next Thurs — tentatively 8/27 10:30am ET. I'll send calendar invites once we have Marcus's pricing sketch.

Thanks team,
Lauren
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
